_affidavit_comment: LetterStream process (--letterstream, legacy alias --affidavits; 8:00 AM daily; renamed from Mailing Affidavits 2026-08-23 — it also sends mailings without affidavits; the affidavit_* key names are unchanged). Generates the Certified Mailing Affidavit from a LetterStream proof-of-mailing PDF and emails it for a YES/NO reply; whoever submitted the request is the affiant named on the affidavit AND its approver (only their YES or James's counts); affidavit_approver (Hailey) is the default for mailings with no known submitter (API pull, --ingest, --fetch, and the affiant name/title fallbacks). affidavit_affiant_titles maps {email: title} for the signature block (default affidavit_affiant_title); user_display_name is James's affiant name for CLI-requested mailings. YES files the affidavit + proof into The Vault. letterstream_api_id/key come from My Account > API Information after LetterStream activates API access. IMPORTANT: LetterStream's documented API (Feb 2023) has NO job-list call, so discovery is '--letterstream --fetch <certified tracking #>' (proof pulled via the API) or '--letterstream --ingest <proof.pdf>' (downloaded by hand); if support ever provides a list call, put its POST params in letterstream_list_params (e.g. {"action": "..."}) and the 8 AM pull becomes automatic — see LETTERSTREAM.md. '--letterstream --probe' verifies auth (accountstatus). affidavit_root blank derives '<cases_root parent>\Mailing Affidavits' (pin it on the Rocky laptop). affidavit_cc is added to every approval email (default: James). affidavit_pdf: convert the approved affidavit to PDF via Word before vaulting (needs Word on the machine; falls back to the .docx).
_affidavit_submit_comment: Primary discovery channel (LetterStream confirmed 2026-08-16 that the API can't list or serve proofs for website-submitted jobs): any firm sender emails rocky@ with affidavit_subject_keyword in the subject and the proof-of-mailing PDF(s) from the LetterStream job page attached; the 8 AM sweep turns each into an affidavit sent back to the submitter for approval (the submitter is the affiant) and replies to the submitter.
_mail_submit_comment: Outbound: Rocky submits certified mail through the LetterStream API. A firm sender emails rocky@ with mail_request_keyword in the subject + ONE PDF (the complete packet); Rocky preauths on LetterStream (nothing bills), emails the requester the recipient + page count + quoted cost tagged [CM-####]; YES from the requester or James releases it (the billing step). NO COST CAP by design (James, 2026-09-21): the LetterStream account's own limits and prepay balance are the ceiling, and no job bills until a human replies YES to an email quoting the exact cost — a second cap in Rocky only refused work the account would have allowed. The legacy mail_max_cost key is ignored. mail_from = the firm return address printed on the envelope/coversheet (defaults in code to the Baltimore office). letterstream_mailtype: 'certified' (with Electronic Return Receipt) or 'certnoerr' (without). Once mailed, the proof is pulled via the API and the affidavit flows automatically.
_mail_batch_comment: BATCHES (2026-09-21): several PDFs on one request email = one mailing per PDF. Each is preauth'd on its own ([CM-####], its own recipient extraction) and all of them are confirmed in ONE [CMB-####] email listing every piece, its cost, and the total; a single YES from the requester (or James) releases the whole batch, a single NO cancels it. A NO on one piece's own [CM-####] drops just that piece and leaves the batch releasable. Two guards, neither about money: mail_batch_max_pieces caps the PDFs one request may carry (default 25), and letterstream_daily_submission_limit guards LetterStream's Method-2 ceiling of 50 API submissions per day — past it, pieces fail with 'resend tomorrow' instead of being silently rejected. CLI: '--letterstream --mail-batch <folder-or-glob>'. Each released piece still produces its own affidavit for its own YES.
_letterstream_extra_comment: Extra POST fields merged into every job submission — the hook for options the Feb 2023 API doc doesn't cover. Pending answer from LetterStream support: the field name for EXPEDITED production (the website's expedite option), which the firm wants as the default; when support names it, add it here (e.g. {"expedite": "1"}) — no rebuild needed. Uploads/job names follow the firm convention 'LastName Matter#' (matter number extracted from the request email; job names carry a short unique suffix).
_litigation_comment: Litigation Updater (--litigation). Bozzuto claims tracking on Smartsheet. smartsheet_token: a Smartsheet API access token (Account > Apps & Integrations > API Access) from an account with access to both sheets. Sheet IDs: File > Properties on each sheet. litigation_root holds the shared data (activity/comms logs, brain.md, voices, report template, the Litigation Update Vault, Reports) — pin it 'Always keep on this device'. Column names are matched by TITLE, so set litigation_entity_column / litigation_closure_column / litigation_disclosure_column / litigation_update_columns to your actual column titles; litigation_update_columns lists the columns updates are normally written into (empty = let Claude use any non-primary column). litigation_entities maps report keys to entity names (report requests: --report BMC or a Teams message 'run a litigation update for BMC'). litigation_audit_reports_dir: folder of PAST audit reports (.docx/.pdf) that teach the third-party-disclosure voice. litigation_summary_column: the internal claim-summary narrative column ('Summary of Claim') — teaches the summary voice. Exemplar documents dropped in <litigation_root>\_litigation\voices\seeds\<updates|summary|closure|disclosure>\ are folded into that voice on every --voice-rebuild as gold-standard references. litigation_notice_senders: mail from (or forwarded from) these addresses is treated as a new legal notice. After a YES executes, the source mail is moved out of rocky@'s inbox into the litigation_processed_folder subfolder (created under the Inbox if missing; set to "" to disable). litigation_mail_move_via: "delegated" (default — rocky@'s cached sign-in, Mail.ReadWrite.Shared, consented 2026-07-05) or "app" (needs Mail.ReadWrite Application). The Teams chat is a persistent group chat titled litigation_chat_topic between rocky@ and litigation_chat_owner (default user_email); litigation_observers may watch but never decide.
_litigation_sheets_comment: TWO open sheets share one closed sheet. Each open-sheet entry: key (shown in chat/logs), sheet_id, entities (routes NEW claims — an incoming notice for one of these entities lands on this sheet), claim_column (the sheet's claim-identifier column), and column_map additions (open->closed title translations layered over the global litigation_column_map). The BCC/BDC master ('BCC_BDC Litigation Report - MASTER', verified 2026-08-02) uses 'Project' where the BMC master uses 'Property Name (State)', and 'Combined Claimant/Project' like the closed sheet. (Legacy single-sheet key litigation_open_sheet_id still works if litigation_open_sheets is absent.)

Its data goes to <mf_tracker_root>\LLT Watch; set llt_watch_root only to override that outright. llt_watch_hours is the inclusive local-hour window the run is allowed in, enforced in code because schtasks can't express a workday-only hourly trigger. llt_watch_ignore_columns suppresses change reports for named columns (empty = report every column, including ones added to the sheet later).

Entity cells hold 'BMC' plus variants like 'B&A d/b/a The Bozzuto Group' — the match lists cover them.
_litigation_closed_comment: Closed sheet ('Closed Claims - MASTER', verified 2026-08-02) mirrors the open sheet plus 'Date Closed' and 'Closure Notes', but three titles drifted — litigation_column_map translates open-sheet titles to closed-sheet titles when a claim moves. Date Closed is auto-set to the move date when the drafted note doesn't carry one.
_litigation_scan_comment: Scanned notices: a PDF with no text layer (a stamped complaint, a faxed demand) has its first litigation_scan_pdf_pages pages attached to the classify/draft calls so Claude reads the pages themselves — the same path the Vault uses, wired in 2026-09-16 after a scanned King County complaint came back as 'text not extractable'. Default 10 (the Vault's 4 is enough to recognize a document; a claims entry needs the allegations). Lower it to trim tokens, raise it if captions and counts routinely run long.
_pacer_monitor_comment: PACER Monitor (--pacer --sync 7:00 AM, --pacer-sweep 6:30 AM, --pacer-digest 5:15 PM, --pacer-mail every monitor cycle). Watches federal dockets through the CourtListener/RECAP API and discovers new cases through the PACER Case Locator. pacer_monitor_root is the shared database folder; blank derives 'PACER Monitor Database' beside Rocky Cases. Pin it 'Always keep on this device' on the Rocky laptop. Authoritative records are JSONL under _db\; the SQLite index (C:\Rocky\pacer\index.db) is derived and rebuilt by --reindex. See PACER_MONITOR.md.
_courtlistener_comment: Free token from courtlistener.com/profile/api/. THE constraint on this whole feature: Free Law Project cut the default authenticated allowance on 2026-05-07 to 5/min, 50/hour, 125/day, and Rocky self-throttles below whatever is set here rather than earning a 429. A FLP membership or commercial agreement raises the cap — raise courtlistener_rate_limits to match when that happens. pacer_resolve_per_run caps how many not-yet-resolved cases spend a lookup call in one run; everything else refreshes in batches of fifty via id__in.
_courtlistener_reserve_comment: Daily calls held back from the SCHEDULED SYNC so interactive work still has budget in the afternoon: an emailed 'send me the docket', a manual --docs, a --probe. At the free tier's 125/day a reserve of 20 leaves the 7:00 AM sync 105. The sync defers whatever it can't reach and queues those cases first next run (they keep their old last_synced on purpose, so nothing starves). 0 disables the reserve.
_pacer_credentials_comment: James's PACER production login. Used two ways: RECAP Fetch (CourtListener drives PACER with these to buy a docket or PDF) and the PACER Case Locator sweeps. PACER forces a password change every 180 days — when a sweep starts failing on 'PACER login refused', that's usually why. pacer_environment 'qa' points at qa-login/qa-pcl with a separate QA account and free test data. pacer_client_code tags billing transactions to a client and is REQUIRED if the account is set to require one (searches fail without it).
_pacer_mfa_comment: PACER made MFA mandatory for CM/ECF-level accounts through 2025, and 'PACER login refused: Invalid username, password, or one-time passcode' means the account has it on. The auth API takes an otpCode field; the codes are ordinary TOTP (6 digits, 30-second window). Paste the BASE32 SECRET KEY that PACER shows beside the QR code in Manage My Account -> multifactor authentication, and Rocky generates each code herself (RFC 6238 on the standard library, no new dependency). An authenticator app holding the same secret keeps working — a TOTP seed can live in as many places as you like. SECURITY: storing this beside the password puts both factors on one machine, which is the ordinary trade for unattended access; the file is local-only and gitignored, and a dedicated PACER login for automation is the cleaner option if you want the factors kept apart. TOTP depends on an accurate clock, so a machine with drifting time fails with 'invalid passcode'.
_pacer_redact_comment: REQUIRED for any PACER account with e-filing privileges — such an account cannot authenticate at all without it, and the failure text is the redaction rule quoted in full. Sending it certifies that the filer complies with Fed. R. App. P. 25(a)(5), Fed. R. Civ. P. 5.2, Fed. R. Crim. P. 49.1, and Fed. R. Bankr. P. 9037 (redact Social Security and taxpayer ID numbers, dates of birth, names of minor children, financial account numbers, and in criminal cases home addresses, in all documents including attachments) — the same attestation CM/ECF collects at every interactive login. Left false on purpose: turning it on is the account holder's act, not Rocky's. Note that PACER Monitor only ever SEARCHES and downloads; nothing here files anything.
_pacer_spend_comment: Money controls. pacer_purchase_enabled false = free RECAP reads only, no billable calls at all. Everything billable draws down pacer_daily_spend_cap: PCL searches report their real fee in the receipt; docket/PDF purchases are recorded at PACER's $3.00 per-document ceiling because the API never reports the actual charge, so the ledger over-states rather than under-states. Every transaction lands in _db\spend.jsonl. pacer_fetch_stale_days = how long RECAP can show no movement on an active case before Rocky buys a fresh docket report.
_pacer_sweeps_comment: Standing party-name searches against the nationwide index — the thing RECAP cannot do. For a landlord-tenant practice this is mostly a bankruptcy tripwire: a tenant filing Chapter 7 or 13 stays the eviction, and PCL sees the filing the day it happens. Each sweep: name (label), party_last_name (also matches entity names), optional party_first_name, jurisdiction_type (ap|bk|cr|cv|mdl), courts (PACER court ids like vaeb/dcb/mdb), bankruptcy_chapters, date_filed_days (rolling window), max_pages (MONEY CONTROL — each page of 54 results is billed), interval_days, auto_watch (add hits to the watchlist automatically), enabled. Sweeps that aren't due are skipped; --sweep --name <sweep> forces one.
_pacer_mail_comment: The team's front door. --pacer-mail scans pacer_mailbox (default rocky_email) for subjects carrying pacer_mail_subject_keyword and answers: watch this case, status, send the docket, send document N. Replies go out guarded (internal addresses only, Level 0 holds — Rocky never sends from James's account). pacer_case_index_seed false stops Rocky reading federal dockets out of Rocky Case Index.xlsx; the index has no docket columns today, so add 'PACER Court' and 'Docket Number' to it and federal matters enroll themselves.
_inbox_cleaner_comment: Inbox Cleaner (--inbox-<key>, e.g. --inbox-matt). Per-user inbox triage that becomes a permanent rule-learning maintenance process. Each key under inbox_users is a process name suffix (inbox-matt, inbox-paul, ...). mailbox must be covered by the Application Access Policy (IT adds it — see INBOX_CLEANER.md). chat_upn defaults to mailbox. Tunables: age_floor_days (case + internal cohorts; newsletters have none), big_cluster_min (thread size before it's 'a big case'), newsletter_min_count / newsletter_max_read_rate (bulk-sender heuristics). inbox_cleaner_dir = the human-facing share folder (rules.md, cohorts, activity + communications logs, review workbook); standard location is 'Rocky Inboxes' under OneDrive Program Files\Rocky (already pinned/synced on the laptop; set the machine's own profile path). Blank = fallback to a 'Rocky Inboxes' folder beside Rocky Cases. Snapshot/moves logs stay LOCAL under C:\Rocky\inbox_cleaner\<key>.
_inbox_observers_comment: observers: extra people in the user's Teams approval chat (group chat instead of 1:1) who can watch and comment — but ONLY the mailbox owner's replies count as approvals. Omit the key to default to [user_email] (James). Set to [] for a true 1:1.
_inbox_write_via_comment: write_via: how --execute authenticates. 'app' (default) = application token, needs Mail.ReadWrite (Application) + admin consent, fenced by the Application Access Policy. 'delegated' = rocky@'s own delegated token (Mail.ReadWrite.Shared, already consented), needs only an Exchange Full Access delegation on the target mailbox — the lighter IT ask, chosen for Matt.
